user.title: NEM Flex Telemetry
user.description: Connect your GitHub account so this household can publish flex telemetry to the cohort dataset. We use GitHub's Device Flow, no passwords or tokens to copy.

show_code.title: Authorise on GitHub
show_code.description:
1. Open https://github.com/login/device in any browser
2. Enter the code: {user_code}
3. Approve access for NEM Flex Telemetry

This window will continue automatically once you approve.

identity.title: Household identity
identity.description: Signed in as {github_login}. The Anonymous household identifier below is a pre-generated UUID v4 with no link to your name, address or GitHub account. Accept the default for the strongest privacy posture, or override with any non-empty label you prefer. Postcode prefix is the first three digits only; the full NMI is never published. See docs/PRIVACY.md in the repo for the threat model.

entities_confirm.title: HAEO entities detected
entities_confirm.description:
Found all required HAEO entities on this instance. Review and confirm, or tick 'Customise mapping' to override.

{detected_entities}

entities_partial.title: Some HAEO entities missing
entities_partial.description: Detected most entities automatically. Please pick the remaining {missing_count} from your sensors below.

data.entity_net_import_kw: Net grid import power (kW, positive = importing)

entities_manual.title: Manual entity mapping
entities_manual.description: HAEO was not detected on this Home Assistant instance, or its entities use non-default names. Please map each schema field to the appropriate sensor. See {haeo_repo} for the reference implementation.

data.entity_net_import_kw: Net grid import power (kW, positive = importing)

consent.title: NEM Flex Telemetry: Privacy and licence
consent.description:
Your data will be published under the [CC-BY-4.0 licence]({licence_url}). Only your postcode prefix (3 digits), NEM region, and the 13 telemetry fields are published. No NMI, no exact location, no appliance data.

See the [privacy statement]({privacy_url}) for full details.

data.opt_in_cohort: Opt in to cohort aggregation (recommended: allows your flexibility to be counted in the community dataset)
data.licence_agreed: I agree to publish my telemetry data under CC-BY-4.0 (required)

reauth_confirm.title: Re-authorise NEM Flex Telemetry
reauth_confirm.description: The GitHub token for {github_login} is no longer valid. Click Continue to re-authorise via Device Flow.

assets.title: Batteries and EVs
assets.description:
How many home batteries and EVs does this household have? Each one gets its own step next, where you map its entities. Any of these may be 0.

Unmapped HAEO entities: {unmapped_entities}

data_description.home_battery_count: Enter 0 if this household has no home battery.
data_description.ev_count: Enter 0 if this household has no EV.
data_description.bidirectional_chargers: Chargers that can also discharge an EV (V2G), shared by the EVs you allow on them. Enter 0 if every EV has a charge-only charger.

asset_battery.title: Home battery: {asset_id}
asset_battery.description: Pick the Home Assistant entities for this battery. Entities found on this instance are pre-filled.

data_description.capacity_kwh: Set to 0 or leave blank if this asset does not exist; it is then left out.
data_description.soc_entity: Required when a capacity is set.

asset_ev.title: EV: {asset_id}
asset_ev.description: Pick the Home Assistant entities for this EV. Entities found on this instance are pre-filled. The plug state is inferred from the shadow price and setpoint. This household has {chargers} bidirectional charger(s).

data.bidirectional_capable: This EV can use the bidirectional charger(s)

data_description.capacity_kwh: Set to 0 or leave blank if this asset does not exist; it is then left out.
data_description.soc_entity: Required when a capacity is set.

no_push_access.title: GitHub account needs write access
no_push_access.description:
Signed in as **{github_login}**, but this account cannot write to `{repo}` yet. Telemetry is pushed straight to that repository, so the maintainer must invite your account first.

Open an issue at {issues_url} titled `[Access request] {github_login}`, then accept the invitation from GitHub.

You can continue setup now. Records are kept for up to 24 hours and pushed once access is granted.
